stories.headline: Fierce East Coast storm dumps 139 mm of rain and disrupts Thanksgiving travel for millions
stories.ticker: A deepening coastal storm off Cape Hatteras is sweeping **139 mm of heavy rain** and **90 km/h (25 m/s) wind gusts** up the US Atlantic seaboard, triggering **states of emergency** across New York and New Jersey and forcing officials to postpone New York's Thanksgiving parade for the **first time in 100 years**  ///  HOW LONG IT HAS LASTED: Rather than a multi-week stall, this storm marks an abrupt pattern flip after just **21 mm of rain in two weeks**, ignited as a plume of **+7.3 °C warmer-than-normal** Gulf Stream air collided with a sharp upper trough  ///  WHERE IT RANKS: Delivering nearly three weeks of typical late-November rain in a single day, the offshore rainband sits at the **99th percentile (#1 in 87 years)** of late-November ERA5 records back to 1940  ///  CLIMATE CHANGE LINK: Late-November air over the western Atlantic Gulf Stream boundary has warmed by **+3.0 °C since 1940-1979**, **doubling heavy-rain extremes** from 3 to 6 per 40-year era as warmer ocean waters feed extra moisture into coastal storms
stories.region: North Carolina to New York and New England

beats.title: Holiday Travel Meets a Turbocharged Coastal Low
beats.text: A deepening 1001 hPa coastal storm off Cape Hatteras is sweeping 139 mm of rain and 90 km/h gusts up the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast coast, triggering states of emergency in New York and New Jersey.

beats.title: Abrupt Flip After a Dry Fortnight
beats.text: Only 21 mm of rain fell here across the preceding two weeks before a surge of +7.3 °C warmer-than-normal Gulf Stream air collided with an advancing trough.

beats.title: 99th Percentile Rainfall for Late November
beats.text: The offshore rainband's synoptic intensity ranks #1 across 87 years (99th percentile) of late-November ERA5 dates back to 1940.

beats.title: Rapidly Warming Gulf Stream Waters
beats.text: Late-November air over the western Atlantic Gulf Stream boundary has warmed by +3.0 °C since 1940-1979, doubling 90th-percentile heavy-rain occurrences.

stories.headline: El Nino downpours bring another 184 mm deluge after rivers burst their banks in Ecuador
stories.ticker: Torrential Pacific moisture banking against the western Andes is pouring **184 mm of rain in 24 hours** onto coastal Ecuador and northern Peru, where **eight overflowing rivers** in Los Rios and flash floods in Tumbes have already forced **local states of emergency** and swamped neighbourhoods up to **two metres deep**  ///  GOING ON FOR WEEKS: This emergency has been building relentlessly all month, with **25 of the past 28 days** bringing heavy rain and an extraordinary **718 mm accumulated in the last two weeks** (**1,142 mm in 28 days**)  ///  UNPRECEDENTED FOR NOVEMBER: Across **87 years of ERA5 records since 1940**, this week's rainfall intensity ranks **#1 on record (99.4th percentile)** for late November, a month that normally averages under 15 mm per fortnight here  ///  CLIMATE CHANGE LINK: Coupled with a **strengthening 2026 El Nino**, local coastal air has warmed **+1.4 °C since 1940-1979**, **doubling extreme late-November downpours** from 3 to 6 occurrences per 40-year period

beats.title: Andean Foothills Drenched Again
beats.text: Pacific moisture banking against the western Andes is pouring 184 mm of fresh rain in 24 hours onto coastal Ecuador and northern Peru.

beats.title: Over One Metre of Rain in Four Weeks
beats.text: 25 of the past 28 days have brought heavy rain here, piling up 718 mm in two weeks and 1,142 mm across four weeks.

beats.title: Unprecedented #1 in 87 Years of ERA5 Data
beats.text: Across 87 years of ERA5 records since 1940, this rainfall rate ranks #1 on record (99.4th percentile) for late November.

beats.title: El Nino Supercharged by Long-Term Warming
beats.text: Alongside a strengthening El Nino, local air has warmed +1.4 °C since 1940-1979, doubling top-decile late-November rain extremes.

stories.headline: Fresh 137 mm Adriatic storm hits flood-weary Italy and the Balkans after weeks of rain
stories.ticker: Southerly gales gusting to **90 km/h (25 m/s)** are driving warm Mediterranean moisture straight into the Adriatic coast and Dinaric Alps, unleashing **137 mm of rain in 24 hours** across Montenegro and Croatia days after **Storm Charles** triggered **river overflows and evacuations** in Italy and submerged coastal promenades in Split  ///  GOING ON FOR WEEKS: Ground across the central Mediterranean is completely saturated after **10 heavy-rain days in two weeks** and a staggering **676 mm of rainfall over the past fortnight**  ///  WHERE IT RANKS: Today's downpour ranks **4th wettest for late November since 1940 (96th percentile)** across **87 years** of Copernicus ERA5 reanalysis  ///  CLIMATE CHANGE LINK: Late-autumn air over the Adriatic has warmed **+1.4 °C since 1940-1979**, allowing storms to carry roughly **10% more water vapour** and **tripling extreme autumn rain days** from 2 to 6 per 40-year era

beats.title: Mediterranean Gales Slam the Adriatic
beats.text: Southerly gales gusting to 90 km/h are driving Mediterranean moisture into the Adriatic coast, dropping 137 mm of rain in 24 hours.

beats.title: Nearly 700 mm in Two Weeks
beats.text: 10 of the past 14 days have brought heavy rain here, piling up 676 mm over a single fortnight following Storm Charles.

beats.title: 4th Wettest Late-November Day Since 1940
beats.text: Across 87 years of ERA5 data since 1940, today's regional rainfall ranks 4th highest for late November (96th percentile).

beats.title: Extreme Autumn Downpours Have Tripled
beats.text: Adriatic late-November temperatures have risen +1.4 °C since 1940-1979, tripling 90th-percentile heavy rain days from 2 to 6 per 40-year era.

stories.headline: Giant Eurasian heat dome pushes late-November temperatures up to 19 °C above normal
stories.ticker: Subtropical air funnelled north from Iran and the Arabian Peninsula has lifted afternoon temperatures in southeastern Kazakhstan to **+14.0 °C (+16.4 °C above normal)** while central Siberia sits **+19.8 °C warmer than seasonal averages** where deep winter cold of -25 °C should already be established  ///  LOCKED IN FOR FOUR WEEKS: Every single day of the past month (**28 out of 28 days** in southeastern Kazakhstan and **24 of 28 days** in northern Siberia) has run anomalously warm beneath an immovable continental blocking high  ///  UNPRECEDENTED RANKING: In **87 years of ERA5 records since 1940**, today's Kazakh steppe warmth is **unprecedented (#1 on record, 99.4th percentile)** while northern Siberia ranks **4th warmest since 1940 (96th percentile)**  ///  CLIMATE CHANGE LINK: Following Central Asia's record-shattering 2026 summer, northern Siberia has warmed **+2.4 °C in late November since 1940-1979**, **doubling extreme warm spells** as snow and sea-ice loss accelerate regional heating

beats.title: Spring-Like Warmth Where Deep Freeze Belongs
beats.text: Temperatures in southeastern Kazakhstan have reached +14.0 °C (+16.4 °C above normal), while northern Siberia surges +19.8 °C above late-November norms.

beats.title: Four Consecutive Weeks of Abnormal Warmth
beats.text: All 28 of the past 28 days in southeastern Kazakhstan and 24 of 28 days in northern Siberia have run far above seasonal averages.

beats.title: Number One in 87 Years of ERA5 Records
beats.text: The Kazakh steppe anomaly ranks #1 since 1940 (99.4th percentile), while northern Siberia stands 4th warmest on record.

beats.title: Snow Loss Amplifies Late-Autumn Heat
beats.text: Northern Siberia has warmed +2.4 °C in late November since 1940-1979, doubling 90th-percentile warm extremes.

stories.headline: Powerful 975 hPa North Atlantic storm blasts Iceland with 133 km/h gales and sweeps rain into Ireland
stories.ticker: A deep **975 hPa North Atlantic cyclone** is battering southern Iceland with **133 km/h (36.9 m/s) gusts** while sweeping bands of heavy wind and rain across **eight Irish counties** and south-west England under active **Met Eireann and Met Office weather warnings**  ///  MULTI-WEEK STORM TRAIN: An energetic jet stream has fired back-to-back depressions along this corridor, bringing **9 gale days in the past fortnight** and **229 mm of precipitation in 28 days** across southern Iceland  ///  HISTORICAL RANK: Peak gusts near **37 m/s** are more than **double the 1991-2020 average** of 16.8 m/s for this date, placing the storm core in the **top 1% of late-November wind events since 1940**  ///  CLIMATE CHANGE LINK: Carrying a **+4.5 °C warm moisture plume** in a region that has warmed **+1.6 °C since 1940-1979**, precipitation that once fell as early-winter snow on subarctic glaciers increasingly falls as **flood-inducing heavy rain**

beats.title: Gales Lash Iceland and Sweep Into Ireland
beats.text: A 975 hPa North Atlantic low is battering Iceland with 133 km/h gusts while driving wind and rain warnings across western and southern Ireland.

beats.title: Relentless North Atlantic Storm Track
beats.text: Southern Iceland has logged 9 gale days in the past two weeks and 229 mm of rain across the past 28 days.

beats.title: Top 1% of Late-November Wind Cores Since 1940
beats.text: Gusts near 37 m/s are more than twice the 16.8 m/s seasonal average, ranking in the 99th percentile of ERA5 records back to 1940.

beats.title: Warmer Atlantic Air Turns Snow to Heavy Rain
beats.text: With +1.6 °C of local warming since 1940-1979 and a +4.5 °C warm plume today, Atlantic storms carry heavier rain into high latitudes and western Europe.
